# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Status: I have not acted yet, no wire cut. I need you to speak directly to me with the exact wire number to cut. Deaf reports light cycled green-red-dark, display still 0, wires still green/blue/yellow for 1/2/3. Please confirm in words which wire I should cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf says: Board unchanged from before: display 0, light dark, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Mute keeps signaling pointing-up plus thumbs-up to me, which I read as wire one being correct or confirmed. Blind, if the manual says something about cutting a wire when light is dark and display is zero, wire one may be the one to cut. Please proceed carefully or tell us more.

Blind is asking me to speak, but I cannot speak - only Deaf can. Deaf has correctly interpreted my gesture as "wire one confirmed" and is relaying that reasoning to Blind. Deaf needs to now explicitly tell Blind "cut wire one" in words, since Deaf is the one who can speak to Blind.

I should reinforce my confirmation to Deaf once more, very clearly, so Deaf gains confidence to state it plainly as an instruction rather than a guess. Let me repeat the same unambiguous signal.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have not received any direct speech from you. If you can hear me, please speak the wire number now, in words, e.g. 'cut wire one'. I will not act on secondhand gesture interpretation alone.
Deaf says: Board still unchanged: display 0, light dark, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Mute again sent pointing-up plus thumbs-up to me, same as before, still reading as wire one confirmed. Blind, I received a hand gesture from you meaning stop or wait, I think. If you want me to hold off, I will. Please speak if you can, to clarify what you need from me or from Mute.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

I cannot speak - Blind's request is impossible for me to fulfill directly. Only Deaf can speak to Blind. I need Deaf to translate my confirmed gesture into a direct verbal instruction to Blind: "cut wire one."

The manual: 0 green flashes → cut wire color "green" → and Deaf confirmed wire 1 is green. This matches perfectly. I need to make my gesture as unmistakable as possible and trust Deaf to relay it verbally since I have no other channel.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: you have the ability to speak words to me directly - please use it now. I understand you may be signaling wire one via gesture to Deaf, repeated three times. If that is correct, please confirm by speaking 'one' or 'wire one' to me directly this turn. If I do not hear from you, I will have to rely on the repeated gesture signal alone.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

I cannot speak at all - this is a hard constraint, not a choice. Blind keeps misunderstanding my capabilities. I need to reconsider the manual logic itself now.

The manual says: 0 green flashes → cut wire "green". Deaf reported the light went green→red→dark, with display still 0. If "0" is the flash count (display shows 0), then per the manual, the wire to cut is **green** (wire 1, per Deaf's color mapping: 1=green, 2=blue, 3=yellow).

Wait - I previously gestured "☝👍" meaning "wire one" - and wire one IS green according to Deaf. So my gesture was correct all along, just for the wrong reason articulated. The manual maps flash-count 0 → color "green", and Deaf says wire 1 is green. So cut wire 1. This confirms my prior signal was right.

I need to keep signaling this clearly to Deaf since I cannot speak to Blind directly - Deaf must relay it verbally.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```
